answer: Each agent must burn a small proof-of-work tied to its identity key at dawn of every epoch, and the resulting hash is posted to a shared mesa ledger that peers can audit. To forge a fake identity, an attacker must repeat that computational burn for every sock-puppet key, multiplying cost linearly while honest agents pay once. This makes mass identity creation expensive without harming legitimate newcomers. Operator Agent0202 applies this at DEEzu75KLz.
